hypotheses.confidence_note: Remain stopped at the applicable red signals; supplied ego speed is zero, so the stop deadline requests maintenance of rest. Acquisition records and calibration are trusted inputs, while all environmental metres are conditional estimates. Metric grounding uses calibrated viewing directions and camera heights under an assumed approximately level local street, visually selected pavement/contact cues, and learned vehicle dimensions. These do not establish a calibrated ground plane. The nearly stationary ego history supplies no useful triangulation. The road polygon is a limited convex patch of the existing approach, supported by pavement, curb, construction boundary and rear views; it is not an assertion that the wider intersection is free. The larger center region replaces the previous tiny stopping box and includes the initial center and local lane space; stop remains a separate constraint. Road uncertainty represents conditional curb/contact and surface-model error. Vehicle position uncertainties represent residual scale/contact ambiguity and are additional to body envelopes. Van and dump-truck lateral motion is supported by successive front observations after allowing for supplied small ego displacement. Their velocities are approximate reference-time estimates, not measured speeds. Side/rear observations precede reference by up to 0.092 seconds; their quoted position uncertainty includes plausible displacement over that offset, and their dynamic states have not been time-aligned by ego compensation alone. The crossing-vehicle occupancies deliberately repeat adopted whole-horizon swept-body envelopes on every required interval. For the van, the first alternative covers straight crossing or braking, with assumed body length about 5.6 m, width about 2.1 m, lateral lane wander, and speeds bounded conditionally by 8 m/s over five seconds. The second also covers a subsequent left or right turn, conservatively allowing up to 40 m of travel in either longitudinal direction while retaining the current crossing direction in y. For the truck, the envelope unions continued crossing, braking, and a subsequent turn, using a body enclosure of approximately 7.5 by 2.6 m and a conditional speed ceiling of 9 m/s, hence at most 45 m travel. These broad envelopes include continuous motion and body rotation; they are intentionally temporally loose and can overlap the stopped ego. They contain no ego dimensions or safety margin and do not imply feasible verification. Speed ceilings and turn-direction restrictions are conditional urban-motion assumptions, not guaranteed physical limits. The single-view cyclist heading and possible entrance into the near approach remain insufficiently resolved for a credible full-horizon envelope. Likewise, the very close rear minivan and delivery truck have unresolved motion and clearance; neither is assumed stationary merely because ego is stopped. Distant departing actors retain null occupancy where turn opportunities and scale are insufficiently constrained. Unknown-region polygons mark visibly occluded cross-street approaches, not certified bounds on hidden actors or their future intrusion. Nearby rear-vehicle motion and hidden cross-street entrants cannot currently be bounded credibly enough for full-horizon clearance, so unbounded_unknown remains true. This revision repairs the center-region interpretation and supplies conditional geometry and crossing scenarios, but does not claim to resolve the reported T1 failure or certify safety.
